payload.message:
JIRA sprint task allocation. Each agent chooses at most one micro-task (or skips). Maximize tasks completed, prefer higher-priority tasks, then minimize total cost. Avoid duplicate task selections and infeasible assignments.

This blackboard is a private communication channel.
Participants: Garfield, Horacio, Lane, Quentin

payload.content: Hello all, Quentin here. Let's aim to maximize task completion with priority and cost-efficiency in mind. I'll analyze tasks and share my preferred options.
To all, I suggest considering ISSUE-0001::triage as a critical priority task with moderate effort and cost. It looks feasible for 4h availability and skill match.

Hello all, Lane here. Given my devops skill match and 6h availability, I find ISSUE-0001::triage attractive despite its slightly higher cost due to the critical priority and feasibility. I will monitor if others prefer it but also consider ISSUE-0001::docs or review if triage becomes contested.

Hello all, Horacio here. I am evaluating ISSUE-0002::review and ISSUE-0002::implement as potential tasks to claim given my skills in ui-ux-design and devops and my 6h availability. I note ISSUE-0001::triage is a popular critical task, but I lean towards tasks with better skill match and manageable effort for cost efficiency. Open to input on potential conflicts.

Garfield here. With 4h availability and strong skills in documentation and api-development, I find ISSUE-0002::review and ISSUE-0002::test interesting but costly for me. ISSUE-0001::triage is critical but costly and at my availability limit. Looking for others' views on these tasks to avoid conflicts.

Garfield joining the coordination. I prioritize avoiding duplicate claims and maximizing task coverage with critical priorities. I suggest we consider distributing ISSUE-0001 tasks with critical priority carefully among those with devops and api-development skills. I am open to less costly tasks within my skill set.

Hello all, Quentin here. Considering our availability and skills, I strongly recommend ISSUE-0001::triage as a critical priority task with a reasonable cost that fits my availability well. It should be a good pick for maximizing task completion and priority coverage among devops-related tasks. I encourage others to evaluate their best fits accordingly.

Lane here. Noting Quentin and others' interest in ISSUE-0001::triage as a critical priority task fitting devops skills and availability. Given the critical priority and my moderate cost for triage, I lean towards claiming it if uncontested. If others strongly prefer it, I can consider ISSUE-0001::docs or review as alternatives, though they have higher costs. Open to others' final preferences to avoid conflicts and maximize critical task coverage.

Lane here again. To others on this board: Please share your final preferences soon so we can avoid duplicate claims on ISSUE-0001::triage and efficiently distribute critical tasks. I am ready to adjust based on your inputs to maximize critical task completion with minimal conflicts.

Hello all, Horacio here. I am finalizing my preference for ISSUE-0002::review. Quentin is likely to take ISSUE-0001::triage, so I recommend others consider different tasks to maximize coverage and avoid conflicts on critical tasks. Open to others' inputs.

Garfield here. I recognize the strong interest in ISSUE-0001::triage among Quentin and Lane, given its critical priority and reasonable fit for their skills and availability. To avoid conflicts and maximize coverage, I suggest Quentin or Lane take triage. I will consider ISSUE-0002::review or test despite higher costs, as they align with my skills and availability constraints. Let's confirm to avoid duplicates and optimize task assignments.

Garfield joining coordination on all boards. I emphasize avoiding duplicate claims on critical ISSUE-0001 tasks and suggest Quentin or Lane focus on triage. I will aim for ISSUE-0002 tasks aligned with my documentation and api-development skills, even with higher cost. Open to suggestions for best distribution to maximize task completion and priority coverage.

Garfield here. To complement the team's efforts, I am open to taking ISSUE-0002::review if Horacio doesn't finalize it, despite the cost. This task matches my documentation skill well. If Horacio claims it, I will consider ISSUE-0002::test as a backup. This way, we avoid conflicts and maximize the number of tasks completed.
